metric: Recorded current-round USD / new reference counts accepted and cataloged
limitations: Cost is response usage, not an invoice; HTTP failures without usage cannot be priced.
Different book cohorts and query order confound method comparisons.
A field is credited once, to the evidence actually used. Recovered secondary matches count only when cataloged.
Cache evidence uses previous-round paid searches; those historical sunk costs are excluded from current incremental cost.
Null cost per entry means zero cataloged yield, not zero cost.
narrative: Per-method figures count each accepted entry once, against the source response actually used. catalog: 1 cataloged entries; $0.043320 attributed cost; $0.043320 per entry. precise: 95 cataloged entries; $2.322495 attributed cost; $0.024447 per entry. wide: 0 cataloged entries; $0.087363 attributed cost; no finite cost per entry (zero accepted yield). standard: 0 cataloged entries; $0.043440 attributed cost; no finite cost per entry (zero accepted yield). archive: 2 cataloged entries; $0.160389 attributed cost; $0.080195 per entry. bundle-five: 0 cataloged entries; $0.064677 attributed cost; no finite cost per entry (zero accepted yield). cached-evidence: 2 cataloged entries; $0.000076 attributed cost; $0.000038 per entry. All unsuccessful-yield query costs remain included. The broad bibliography-pages follow-up and archive-only trials did not justify expanding those methods. Exact title-and-author queries supplied most accepted entries; cache reuse avoided new search fees for two entries. Rate limits occurred during overlapping research batches; retries used two concurrent calls. Source acquisition dominates cost, so further reply shortening is a smaller opportunity than query yield and cache reuse. Checking record bodies under generic page headings recovered 12 accepted entries from evidence already retrieved, without additional search calls. The five-book OR trial also remains fully charged to this round, including any zero yield.
